concept: Queryable Encryption ESC/ECOC metadata compaction and leakage tradeoffs
summary: Source-anchored research for Queryable Encryption ESC/ECOC metadata compaction and leakage tradeoffs. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: MongoDB documents manual metadata compaction, recommends running it when metadata exceeds 1 GB, and exposes compactStructuredEncryptionData with per-field compactionTokens and a mongosh wrapper. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
MongoDB recommends manual metadata compaction above 1 GB; treat that operational threshold together with the scheduling leakage warning. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

MongoDB documents omission of compactStructuredEncryptionData and other encrypted-collection operations from the slow query log and system.profile; this reduces diagnostic visibility and is not a claim that every log channel is protected. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

SERVER-128430 describes concurrent writes racing with ECOC rename/recreation during cleanup or compaction. On sharded clusters, implicit ECOC creation can fail inside a distributed transaction. The ticket was updated October 5, 2026; its listed versions and resolution do not prove every later build is affected. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05)

MongoDB excludes persistent adversaries and adversaries possessing both database snapshots and accompanying query transcripts/logs from Queryable Encryption security guarantees. Its documented redaction omits compactStructuredEncryptionData from the slow query log and profiler on encrypted collections. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
QE maintains ESC and ECOC metadata collections alongside the encrypted collection; Go driver integration tests explicitly check their creation. (medium confidence)

For equality-indexed fields, each insert or update adds one ESC write and one ECOC write per indexed field. Before compaction, each metadata collection stores one document per indexed field/value occurrence. (low confidence)
Metadata compaction empties ECOC and reduces ESC by removing redundant metadata documents; compactStructuredEncryptionData is the dedicated command. (medium confidence)
MongoDB warns that compaction can, in the worst case, reveal how many unique field/value pairs were inserted since the previous compaction. (low confidence)

The documented scheduling rule for removing at least t ESC documents is (encfields × docinserts) − valinserts ≥ t, with valinserts counting unique field/value pairs since the last compaction. (low confidence)
The documented workflow runs compaction manually through an encryption-configured mongosh client; the command accepts field-to-compaction-token mappings. (medium confidence)

The ETH Zurich analysis published in June 2023 studied the MongoDB 6.0 public-preview design, including an ECC collection absent from the current two-collection description. Its compaction attack assumes access to an operation-log snapshot after compaction and a similarly distributed auxiliary plaintext dataset; statistical attack evaluation used simulated leakage. These are historical results, not verification against current releases. (low confidence)

MongoDB excludes persistent adversaries and attackers with snapshots plus query transcripts/logs from QE security guarantees. The ETH attack illustrates why log-inclusive compromise needs separate assessment. (medium confidence)

MongoDB engineering issue SERVER-92399 describes range-compaction padding documents added to ESC to reduce leakage of real anchor documents. It reports an unsigned-underflow problem in unit-test padding calculations; this record does not establish a deployed production exploit. (low confidence)

SWiSSSE proposes evaluating leakage across both encrypted indexes and encrypted documents. Its research constructions combine response-volume bucketization, delayed pseudorandom write-backs, and indistinguishable searches and updates; these are research techniques, not documented MongoDB compaction options. (low confidence)

MongoDB creates enxcol_.<collectionName>.esc and enxcol_.<collectionName>.ecoc alongside an encrypted collection. These metadata structures and __safeContent__ must not be manually altered. (low confidence)
